name: Gastroparesis

criteria.description: Upper GI symptoms suggestive of gastric retention (nausea, vomiting, early satiety, postprandial fullness, bloating)
Objective evidence of delayed gastric emptying (scintigraphy: > 10% retention at 4 hours)
Absence of mechanical gastric outlet obstruction (confirmed by upper endoscopy or imaging)
Wireless motility capsule showing delayed gastric emptying

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Symptoms of delayed gastric emptying, objective documentation of delayed emptying on gastric scintigraphy (>10% retention at 4 hours using standardized meal), and exclusion of mechanical obstruction.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diabetic gastroparesis accounts for ~33% of cases; idiopathic ~36%; post-surgical ~13%. Medications affecting motility must be stopped before testing.

pathognomonic.notes: Most common symptom; often persistent and debilitating

pathognomonic.symptomName: Vomiting of undigested food hours after eating
pathognomonic.notes: Vomitus contains recognizable food eaten hours earlier

common.notes: Epigastric predominant; correlates poorly with emptying rate

occasional.notes: Unpredictable absorption of nutrients leads to glycemic variability

rare.notes: Severe cases may require enteral or parenteral nutrition

laboratory: Nutritional deficiencies (iron, vitamin D, B12) in severe cases
imaging: 4-hour gastric emptying scintigraphy (gold standard): >10% retention at 4 hours is abnormal
CT abdomen to exclude mechanical obstruction
Upper GI series may show retained food/barium in stomach
genetic: No established single-gene cause for most cases
SCN5A sodium channel variants identified in some idiopathic cases
other: Upper endoscopy: retained food in fasting stomach, no mechanical obstruction
Wireless motility capsule (SmartPill) as alternative to scintigraphy
Gastric electrical activity testing (electrogastrography) may show dysrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: SMA syndrome causes duodenal rather than gastric obstruction
CT angiography shows narrowed aortomesenteric angle in SMA syndrome
CIPO involves diffuse intestinal dysmotility beyond stomach
CIPO shows dilated bowel loops on imaging
CVS has episodic pattern with symptom-free intervals
Gastric emptying is typically normal between episodes in CVS

redFlags: New-onset gastroparesis in patient > 55 years (exclude malignancy)
Severe dehydration or electrolyte imbalance from intractable vomiting
Bezoar formation causing complete gastric outlet obstruction
Recurrent diabetic ketoacidosis from erratic glucose control
references: Camilleri M, et al. ACG Clinical Guideline: Gastroparesis. Am J Gastroenterol. 2013;108(1):18-37.
Parkman HP, et al. American Gastroenterological Association technical review on the diagnosis and treatment of gastroparesis. Gastroenterology. 2004;127(5):1592-1622.
Lacy BE, et al. AGA Clinical Practice Update on Management of Medically Refractory Gastroparesis. Gastroenterology. 2022;162(6):1762-1774.
